source_text: Ὅτι δὲ καὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν γενόμενος ἄνθρωπος παθεῖν καὶ ἀτιμασθῆναι ὑπέμεινε καὶ πάλιν μετὰ δόξης παραγενήσεται, ἀκούσατε τῶν εἰρημένων εἰς τοῦτο προφητειῶν. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Ἀνθ᾿ ὧν παρέδωκαν εἰς θάνατον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ τῶν ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη, αὐτὸς ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν εἴληφε καί τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐξιλάσεται. Ἴδε γὰρ συνήσει ὁ παῖς μου, καὶ ὑψωθήσεται καὶ δοξασθήσεται σφόδρα. Ὃν τρόπον ἐκστήσονται πολλοὶ ἐπὶ σέ, οὕτως ἀδοξήσει ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπων τὸ εἶδός σου καὶ ἡ δόξα σου ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οὕτως θαυμάσονται ἔθνη πολλά, καὶ συνέξουσι βασιλεῖς τὸ στόμα αἰτῶν· ὅτι οἷς οὐκ ἀνηγγέλη περὶ αὐτοῦ ὄψονται, καὶ οἳ οὐκ ἀκηκόασι συνήσουσι. Κύριε, τίς ἐπίστευσε τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη; Ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ ὡς παιδίον, ὡς ῥίζα ἐν γῇ διψώσῃ. Οὐκ ἔστιν εἶδος αὐτῷ οὐδὲ δέξα· καὶ εἴδομεν αὐτόν, καὶ οὐκ εἶχεν εἶδος οὐδὲ κάλλος, ἀλλὰ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἄτιμον καὶ ἐκλεῖπον παρὰ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους. Ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὢν καὶ εἰδὼς φέρειν μαλακίαν, ὅτι ἀπέστραπται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, ἠτιμάσθη καὶ οὐκ ἐλογίσθη. Οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐλογισάμεθα αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν πόνῳ καὶ ἐν πληγῇ καὶ ἐν κακώσει. Αὐτὸς δὲ ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν· παιδεία εἰρήνης ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν, τῷ μώλωπι αἰτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν. Πάντες ὡς πρόβατα ἐπλανήθημεν, ἄνθρωπος τῇ ὁδῷ αὐτοῦ ἐπλανήθη· καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν ταῖς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν, καὶ αὐτὸς διὰ τὸ κεκακῶσθαι οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείροντος αὐτὸν ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. Ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη“. Μετὰ οἶν τὸ σταυρωθῆναι αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ γνώριμοι αὐτοῦ πάντες ἀπέστησαν, ἀρνησάμενοι αὐτόν· ὕστερον δέ, ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντος καὶ ὀφθέντος αὐτοῖς καὶ ταῖς προφητείαις ἐντυχεῖν, ἐν αἷς πάντα ταῦτα προείρητο γενησόμενα, διδάξαντος, καὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον ἰδόντες καὶ πιστεύσαντες καὶ δύναμιν ἐκεῖθεν αἰτοῖς πεμφθεῖσαν παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λαβόντες καὶ εἰς πᾶν γένος ἀνθρώπων ἐλθόντες, ταῦτα ἐδίδαξαν καὶ ἀπόστολοι προσηγορεύθησαν.
pass_a_gloss: That He also became a man for us, and suffered and was dishonored, and will come again with glory, hear the prophecies spoken for this purpose. For it is written: 'For the sake of the fact that He gave His soul to death, and He was counted among the lawless, He Himself bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the lawless. For my servant will understand, and He will be exalted and greatly glorified. Just as many will be astonished at You, so Your appearance will be dishonored among men, and Your glory among men, so many nations will marvel, and kings will shut their mouths in amazement; for those who have not been told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.' 'Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We have told it to Him as to a child, as a root in dry ground. He has no form or beauty; and we saw Him, and He had no form or beauty, but His appearance was dishonored and lacking among men.' A man in suffering, knowing how to bear weakness, because His face was turned away, He was dishonored and not esteemed. This One bears our sins and suffers for us, and we thought He was in pain and in suffering and in evil. But He was wounded for our lawlessness and bruised for our sins; the punishment for our peace was upon Him, and by His bruise we were healed. All we like sheep have gone astray, each man to his own way; and the Lord gave Him over to our sins, and He did not open His mouth because of our evil. Like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer, He was silent; thus He did not open His mouth. In His humiliation His judgment was taken away. After He was crucified and all who knew Him denied Him, later, after He rose from the dead and appeared to them, and they encountered the prophecies in which all these things were spoken as going to happen, and He taught them, and they saw Him ascending into heaven, and they believed, and they received power sent from there by Him, and they came to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.
pass_b_english: Now hear the prophecies spoken for this very purpose: that He also became a man for our sake, endured suffering and dishonor, and will come again in glory (Isaiah 53). It is written: "Because He surrendered His life to death and was numbered among the lawless, He Himself bore the sins of many and will make atonement for the lawless. For My Servant will understand, and He will be exalted and greatly glorified. Just as many were astonished at You — so Your appearance was dishonored among men and Your glory among men — so many nations will marvel, and kings will shut their mouths in amazement; for those who have not been told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand. Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We announced Him before Him as a child, as a root in dry ground. He has no form or splendor; we saw Him, and He had no form or beauty, but His appearance was dishonored and lacking among men. A man in suffering, knowing how to bear weakness, because His face was turned away, He was dishonored and not esteemed. This One bears our sins and suffers for us, and we considered Him to be in pain, in suffering, and in affliction. But He was wounded for our lawlessness and bruised for our sins; the punishment for our peace was upon Him, and by His bruise we were healed. All of us like sheep have gone astray, each man to his own way; and the Lord gave Him over to our sins, and because He was afflicted He did not open His mouth. Like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer He was silent; thus He did not open His mouth. In His humiliation His judgment was taken away." After He was crucified, all who knew Him withdrew and denied Him. But later, after He rose from the dead and appeared to them, and they encountered the prophecies in which all these things were foretold as destined to happen, and He taught them, and they saw Him ascending into heaven, and they believed, and they received power sent from there by Him, and they went to every nation of men, they taught these things and were called apostles.
